- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 20-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns positive (≥ 0.1) after a dip, model may underreact; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to forecast.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, model tends to drift upward; apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction for next 7 days.
